why: LSP 3.17 textDocument/definition: a call resolves to the function defined with name() syntax. bash manual, SIMPLE COMMAND EXPANSION: "the first word is taken to be the name of the command"; COMMAND EXECUTION: "If there exists a shell function by that name, that function is invoked". the first word is the command name, looked up as a function first.

LSP 3.17 textDocument/definition: call inside another function resolves to the definition made with the function keyword and no parentheses. bash manual, SHELL GRAMMAR, Shell Function Definitions: both forms define a function.
bash manual, SHELL GRAMMAR, Shell Function Definitions: 'function name ()' is the combined form.
Sequential execution (bash manual, SHELL GRAMMAR, Lists): the definition command runs before the call that follows it, so the first call sees the first definition only.
Sequential execution (Lists): the second definition command has run before the second call and replaced the first, so only it is in effect.
Sequential execution (Lists): the definition inside outer runs when outer's body runs, before the call that follows it.

bash manual, FUNCTIONS: 'Function names and definitions may be listed with the -f option to the declare' and removed with unset -f, with no scope qualifier; the table is shell-wide, so after outer has run inner is callable at top level.
bash manual, SHELL BUILTIN COMMANDS, unset: 'unset -f' removes the function, so the last call has no definition.
bash manual, COMMAND EXECUTION: 'If there exists a shell function by that name, that function is invoked' before builtins are searched.
bash manual, SHELL BUILTIN COMMANDS, builtin: 'Execute the specified shell builtin', so 'builtin cd /' calls the builtin and not the function; the plain call 'cd /tmp' is a reference.
bash manual, SHELL BUILTIN COMMANDS, command: 'Run command with args suppressing the normal shell function lookup'; the plain call 'cd /tmp' is a reference.
bash manual, SHELL GRAMMAR, Compound Commands, if: only one branch runs, chosen by $FAST at run time, so either definition can be the one in effect; one of the two must be offered.
bash manual, source: only commands executed in a shell define functions; this file does not source dup_b.sh, so that shell never has the other twin.
Same as the sibling file: dup_a.sh is never sourced here.
bash manual, PARAMETERS: a variable is set by assignment; LIMIT has one assignment, so the read inside a function binds to it.
